Neuro-linguistic programming is a largely discredited pseudoscience that claims to be able to "reprogram" the human brain via auditory stimulation.

Its creators claimed that NLP can treat problems such as phobias, depression, habit disorder, psychosomatic illnesses, myopia, allergy, common cold, and learning disorders.

As /u/g33k3ss said: If you would like a highly entertaining fictionalized account of what NLP is, check out Snow Crash; it's a great book.

I'm going to post an answer. I have no idea if this answer is correct, but it's my current working definition, based on the solid foundation of totally personal and anecdotal evidence, and not even bothering to seriously read up on the subject. I am posting this answer knowing that if it's wrong, there's no better way to get a correct answer on the Internet than to post an incorrect answer:

NLP is a bunch of tricks, some old, some not so old, that people use to manipulate others, generally for selfish reasons, packaged as "scientific technique" and sold as a great tool for managers, negotiators, salesmen, and the like – i.e. it's guilt-free packaging for things people do to pull a fast one on you.

Don't wast your time. It's total bullshit. A scam cooked up by this guy and a few others. They twisted a few of the ideas of Milton Erickson - who was a genius - to create something to sell self help merchandise. They cashed in on the people looking for new age crap with a pseudo-scientific feel.

If it moves you, go straight to Milton Erickson. You'll understand the ides these clowns took and used for their scam and a whole lot more.

NLP is essentially a codified way of manipulating other people. Can it cure depression and phobias? Likely not. Can it get you to buy a car you don't necessarily want? Ask a car salesman. Can it get you to vote a certain way without really understanding why? Ask a political strategist.

Most airing anime should have aired their third episode at this point. The third episode is typically the cut-off point people use when judging whether to stay with or drop an anime. In this thread, I invite everyone who has watched an an anime to it's third episode to drop a comment and tell people if it's worth watching.

I would love to avoid spoilers, but if it's unavoidable, please make sure to tag the spoiler in the format mentioned in the sidebar.
Shimoneta to Iu Gainen ga Sonzai Shinai Taikutsu na Sekai — great comedy if you ok with overload of obscene jokes and innuendos. Also, got sort of Fahrenheit 451 and 1984 vibe from it.

The thing about the obscene jokes is in their delivery - the comedy doesn't lie in the "Haha, she said ride me as a double entendre!" it's the context within the show itself regarding the delivery of that line. It's a very loving satire of the moral-guardianship and taboos that are very present in Japan/anime/media in general, much in the same vein as Animaniacs

Gate, Gangsta, Aoharu x Kikanjuu and Rokka. Arslan Senki and World Trigger are also pretty good if we count continuing shows.

Gate surprised me, didn't think I'd like it this much but the concept of Modern Weapons vs Fantasy is pretty cool. Pick it up if that interests you, other than that it doesn't have much to offer.

Rokka's concept is weaker but the characters are stronger. I love the interactions between the rokka no yuusha. Its the basic tale of good vs evil, if it wasn't for the strong characters it would be one of the worst animes this season. Cool MC, interesting characters. If you like that, then this is the show for you.

Aoharu x Kikanjuu is a lovely character study of wierd almost out of this world people with exagerated personalities. The show is based around a airsoft team that is created because of... circumstances... It's fun and light hearted. I like it alot so far.

Gangsta is overall pretty strong and shows great promise, but has been kinda slow so far compared to Black Lagoon for example. If you liked Black Lagoon you'll probably like this one. Hard to talk about it without spoiling things.

World Trigger is just fun to watch, it's a typical shounen but better than most of the popular ones. Interdimensional war, fun characters and pretty decent fight scenes.

Arslan Senki is fantastic for someone like me who loves tactics and battles. It's draw comes from that and character interactions mostly. It's not too late to catch up if you're into that sort of thing.

World trigger is something that will be popular in a year in the west and everyone will get sick of hearing about it. I'll just enjoy it in peace until then.

It's seriously one of the best long running shows that no one seems to be aware of yet. I don't really count it as this season since it's on episode 39. It's weird to think it's already been airing that long.

Arslan Senki (Cont) - Still going strong, and great stuff if you enjoy large scale battles and tactics mixed with a bit of politics.

Gangsta - Probably one of top contenders for AotS right now. It's got a bit of a slow pace, but the slow build has been very interesting to me at the very least.

Ranpo Kitan: Game of Laplace - This is one of the stranger anime this season, but enjoyable none the less. I do think the eccentric nature of the show will turn some off, as well as the macabre nature of most of the mysteries they've worked one. If you don't mind that kind of stuff though, it's a fun watch.

Gate - This one has me with mixed feelings. I like the concept, I've enjoyed the overall experience of fantasy vs. modern warfare, however the main character leaves me conflicted. I get a lot of people defending things I've critiqued, but I think the strength in this anime comes from it's battles over it's characters, at least for the time being.

Chaos Dragon - The train wreck opening of the season. I do think it's improved itself, at least enough not to be dropped, but the first episode is just a mess. The show itself is lacking, with the MC being it's biggest weakness. Luckily the side characters are interesting enough to stick around, but considering the nature of the show, that might not last.

Aoharu x Kikanjuu - This show is meant for just pure fun in my opinion. I don't think the actual plot is what will make people watch. The characters are fun to enjoy, and the reverse trap has been quite fun due to the situations she's found herself in. I wouldn't expect any major plot elements, just a lot of fun character interactions.

Ushio to Tora - This anime caught me off guard, as I only started it after I stumbled upon the OP on youtube and loved it enough to give it a shot. It's definitely worth the look. I think the obvious parallel is Inuyasha, but without the boy/girl relationship going on. So it's just good natured fun at this point.

DRRR!!X2 - This of course requires seeing the prior seasons, but it's definitely worth picking up if you have. I think it's a step up from the last arc so far and the intrigue is really interesting to follow. So if you're a fan of the series it's definitely worth following.

Rokka no Yuusha - I always enjoy these basic demon king vs. the heroes stories, so I actually had pretty high expectations going in. So far it's delivered on everything I could want, good characters, and decent action. I look forward to the drama that's to come when all the characters are revealed.

Overlord - My personal favorite for the season. Albedo being the cream on top for an intelligent show focusing on the 'bad guy'. I'm always a sucker for the stuck in an MMO concept, but this is delivering in a way that SAO and LH didn't. So hopefully it stays strong.

Chopping Block - Chaos Dragon & God Eater, these are the two shows I'm currently considering dropping. I'll post further thoughts on God Eater once the third episode has aired.

Gakkou Gurashi!: AOTS, quite possibly AOTY. It's just great. If you haven't watched episode 1 yet, I advise you to just open Crunchyroll and watch it right now. Don't see its MAL/AniList/Hummingbird page before, it spoils episode 1.

Classroom Crisis: Ehh. It's not terrible, but it hasn't showed its meat yet (if it ever will). I think episode 4 will be a make it or break it point for it.

Charlotte: Best OP ever. Show is good, but the serious parts could have more impact while the humor (IMO) should have been worked on more.

Durarara!!x2 Ten: I have no strong feelings towards it, the show is not for me. However, after watching 37 episodes before x2 Ten aired, I feel like I'm in too far to drop it.

Gangsta.: I'm not sure how much I like the superpower-ness of dogtags here. Besides that it's really good, and having adults as MCs is a really refreshing change of pace.

GATE: Pretty disappointed in the censorship, I haven't read it seems like the manga was much better with this. First episode wasn't too good, but the last 2 were just fine.

Monster Musume: Why do I keeping watching this. Why do I keep watching this. I'm most likely going to drop it next episode. This is a show where I can't help but be disappointed in. How many shows have clearly non-human main characters? Not very many. Seeing how mythical and not-so mythical (jellies...) species interact with human society would be interesting. Using it as a backdrop for a generic ecchi harem is not.

Overlord: Feels similar to Log Horizon, but this one has actual violence! One of the shows I look forwards to every week, and I love having a non-human-looking MC.

Ranpo Kitan: Weird is the best word to describe it. Writings pretty bad but the shows weirdness manages to keep me watching.

Rokka no Yuusha: The monster CGI is absolutely terrible, rest of the show is really good. Setting is also really interesting, I haven't seen any anime with a Mayan (or Native American in general) setting before.

Shimoneta to Iu Gainen ga Sonzai Shinai Taikutsu na Sekai: Possibly the funniest anime I've watched yet, and under a message of anti-government censorship. I think its great.

Chaos Dragon: Animation's pretty (except for those eye designs), show is shit. I've dropped it on episode 3.

Ushio to Tora: I'm not interested in shounen battles or 90s shows, so I'm not really interested in it. If you do like any of those things then this will be great for you.

God Eater: Still on episode 2.

Fate/Kaleid Liner Prisma Illya 2wei Herz: Not even aired yet -.-

Joukumachi no Dandelion, Kuusen Madoushi Kouhosei no Kyoukan: Dropped those on episode 2, the former is boring and the second is a generic harem.

For my recommendations, I'm sticking to shows which debuted this season. No sequels or carry-over shows from last season. I tried my best to avoid spoilers in these, but I do apologise if I accidentally did

Akagami no Shirauki-hime

Whilst this show may be based on a childern’s fairytale, it doesn’t feel childish at all. From what has been shown of the show so far, this feels like a really nice drama show. The main two characters are enjoyable to watch, they have a great charisma between the two of them and they each have their own strengths and weaknesses which the show has made good use of so far. The main plot has only been really introduced now and I’m not exactly sure what is going to end up happening with the rest of the season, but from the stories shown so far in the show, I’m looking forward to seeing where this one goes. I’d recommend this show for anyone looking for a drama show this season

Charlotte

Whilst this show has turned into a favourite of many, this show hasn’t completely captured my interest yet. As much as it is a comedy, I’m starting to see jokes repeat themselves, not that many but still noticeable and they didn’t make me laugh that much the second time around. I do find the segments of the show with the student council finding the people with special powers part to be good, but I'm still not sold on the emotional parts of the show yet, and I feel like as the show is going to go on, we're going to see less and less of those parts and the show is going to solely focus on the main characters and the emotional journey they'll go through, and I haven't exactly been sold on those parts yet. YMMV with this one

Gangsta

If you’re looking for an action show for this season which isn't quite fantasy-based, this show is going to be your best. The action scenes that have been showed so far have been really nice, and each character’s combat style does end up being quite differentiated, which makes for some enjoyable scenes. There really hasn’t been that much of an over-arching plot so far within the show, as the show is mainly focusing on the relationship between the two main characters, but that does seem rather interesting (though, I’d be lying if I said I didn’t want an overarching plot which would somewhat tie into the flashbacks). So far, I’d recommend picking this one up. On another note, it also has the best OP of the season

Overlord

This show hasn't catched my attention so far, and I'm finding myself pretty bored when I'm watching it. I’ve seen the whole “people from real world gets transported into a game world” idea a number of times already, but this show hasn’t done a lot to differentiate it for me. None of the characters have really stood out for me so far, the main plot hasn’t done anything particularly interesting. The setting hasn’t had anything particularly strong to it. This show just feels like a generic action show to me. I’ve dropped this, but I suppose YMMV with this one due to other people’s opinion about this

Rokka no Yuusha

This is one of my more favourite shows so far this season. The action has been enjoyable to watch, and the aztec setting for this hasn’t been particularly used so far, so the setting has got that uniquity to it. These first few episodes have been filled with world-building (most notably, a big chunk of the first episode dedicated to it), but I feel that they weren’t that boring to get through. The description for the show is promising some mystery elements to the show which have started to show in episode 3, which I’m excited to see how it goes. Just in case I’d recommend this

Charlotte is definitely worth watching! Especially if you like Angel Beats. Now while its hard to say if it will be better than Angel Beats, its sure starting to seem that way. Charlotte is definitely hitting all the buttons it wants to hit and certainly is resonating with me!

WARNING RANT ALERT I don't get why everyone isn't seeing the masterful storytelling that is occurring in Charlotte. It easily the most thought out show this season and probably has more to say than everything else too. Charlotte demands its audiences attention and isn't willing to give things away very easily. So it does take a little bit more thought to figure out whats really going on what people are trying to say. But the things to be found are developing into real gems. Since everyone else is so into the term AOTS, I'd like to officially declare Charlotte as such. If you're looking for something more than afternoon junk food, this show will not disappoint.

I'm really enjoying this season but I don't see a new killer app we'll be talking about in 10 years this season like I did last with Kekkai Sensen.The new shows I see as having the most potential are:

  • Gate
  • Charlotte
  • Monmusu
  • Overlord
  • Rokka

Monmusu is probably the strongest contender for a cult following. Charlotte has a chance to be the next AB, but not the next Clannad from what I've seen so far. I hope I'm wrong but it seems to just be missing something to hit critical mass.Gate has a cool concept and story, but it's up to the studio to light the spark. Overlord is a radical power fantasy, those are hit or miss but sometimes manage to light up mid season or get a cult following for years. Ushio to Tora is amazing and probably my favorite thing this season but I can't really judge how well others will flock to it. Rokka is going to come down to execution. If it doesn't drop the ball I see it getting pretty popular.

The more niche anime I'm enjoying are:

  • Shinmota
  • Himouto
  • Joukamachi
  • Wakaba Girls
  • Okusama ga Seitokaichou!
  • Jitsu wa watashi wa
  • Aoharu

I don't think Himouto will get very big with the mainstream but I can almost guarantee it a cult following. Shinmota completely relies on your individual sense of humor, but I enjoy it because it reminds me of the mid 2000's crude humor gag anime that we used to get so much of (e.g. Inukami!). Joukamachi and Wakaba girls are slice of life anime which you need to buy into the characters like in the first place. I think they're enjoyable with no major faults. Jitsu wa watashi wa is a personal favorite of mine this season because of the nonstandard character design which reminds me a of oniichan no koto...'s non standard style, but a lot less perverse. Okusama and Danchigai exist as ecchi short but they're not gonna be a conversation starter. Okusama seems to be hitting the right notes though. Aoharu is a nice survival game with some classic genderbender elements anime. It is not really entry level at all and I could see a lot of people being turned off by it but I find it enjoyable. It reminds me of classics like Nononononononono.

The sequel seasons I'm watching are:

  • Non Non Biyori
  • Cinderella Girls
  • Working
  • Gatchaman

They're all really strong, but you should already know if you like them. Gatchaman's plot isn't doing it for me.The whole thing seems really flippant and ungrounded. Stuff just happens with little thought and the plot flops around like a fish. There don't seems to be rules. Worst off the crowds are still the primary enemies which is getting so tired. It's not terrible and looks really great just those issues rub me the wrong way.

Biggest Disappointments:

  • God Eater
  • Ranpo Kitan
  • Chaos Dragon

Favorite Show:

  • Ushio to Tora

Ranpo was offensive to me. They didn't even bother giving the viewers clues or a chance to figure the "mystery" out. They introduced the murder and the motives after they solved the case. Scooby doo is a better mystery show. That leaves its thriller aspect as the fallback for its premise, but it's nothing I haven't seen before. Maybe if I hadn't been an internet denizen for so long the human furniture would have given me a gut check instead of a chuckle (thanks weird furniture fetish people). God eater contradicted itself at every turn and the stiff CG showed through. It's basically the opposite of Ushio to Tora in that regard. It's very sad considering UFOtable just came off the excellent remake of UBW. Chaos dragon annoys me for the same reason Gatchaman does, it just feels to flip from scene to scene. The attempts at provoking emotion are offensive and primitive too. At least the designs are nice.

Ushio to Tora is my favorite show this season by a margin. Maybe I'm just a sucker for the aesthetics or the nostalgia but I can't wait for it every week.The last episode specifically sealed the deal for me. It looks fantastic in every shot. The storyline is simple but non offensive, which is some times best. I'm also enjoying the character development and again the non-standard (more like old standard) design.
